name: Stephen Steinle
bio: I am a computer science Ph.D. student in the Advancing Machine and Human Reasoning Lab at the University of South Florida. My research focuses on conversational strategic reasoning, natural language processing, and cognitive modeling: how people and language models reason, explore ideas, and make decisions.

My work spans persona-based evaluation, semantic exploration, legal retrieval and entailment, and syntax-guided code generation. I also bring applied experience from Amazon Ring, the Air Force Research Laboratory, and CACI, alongside seven years of service in the United States Navy.

experience.organization: AMHR Lab, University of South Florida
details: Develop NLP and large language model methods for strategic dialogue, including stance, goal, and strategy inference from conversational context.
Design controlled reasoning evaluations to identify the effects of missing information, constraints, and prompting assumptions.

experience.organization: Amazon | Hawthorne, California, United States | On-site
details: Built a Python/AWS pipeline that evaluates AI coding-agent sessions, identifies failure patterns, generates corrective lessons, validates them through A/B replay experiments, and publishes approved lessons back into agent memory.
Developed a multi-stage evaluator for AI coding-agent sessions, combining deterministic transcript parsing with LLM-based classification and structured JSON validation.
Built failure-detection workflows to identify stumbles in tool-use cycles, extract surrounding context, and classify behavior with confidence scoring.
Implemented a learner pipeline that converts failures into lessons, clusters recurring patterns using embeddings, TF-IDF, and HDBSCAN, and synthesizes canonical guidance.
Designed A/B replay validation to compare control vs. lesson-injected agent behavior, measuring prevention-rate deltas with statistical tests and confidence intervals.
Resulted in a favorable internship evaluation and an inclination to hire.
Technologies: Bedrock, S3, DynamoDB, CloudWatch, EventBridge, ECS Fargate, and AgentCore Memory.
Built repository and documentation search using LLM-expanded keyword retrieval and query-focused document summaries.
Implemented an MCP service connecting Cursor with OpenSearch queries and keyword-usage summaries.
Implemented anomaly-detection workflows over vehicle traffic data to support investigation and triage.
Built a natural-language action legality system that maps utterances to structured actions and checks permissibility against a ruleset and game state.
Performed cyber intelligence and cybersecurity operations, including incident response and network auditing.
